categories.main_business_segments: Cleveland-Cliffs operates primarily through its Steelmaking segment, which encompasses the mining of iron ore, production of steel, and downstream finishing, stamping, tooling, and tubing. Other operating segments include Tubular, Tooling and Stamping, and European Operations, but the vast majority of revenue and assets are concentrated in Steelmaking. The company is vertically integrated, controlling the supply chain from raw materials to finished steel products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes both blast furnace/basic oxygen furnace (BF/BOF) and electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking technologies, supported by its own iron ore mining, pelletizing, and hot briquetted iron (HBI) production. Advanced high-strength steel (AHSS), electrical steels (GOES and NOES), and coated steels are produced using proprietary metallurgical processes and continuous innovation at its Research and Innovation Center. Cleveland-Cliffs also operates scrap processing, cokemaking, and coal mining facilities to support its steel production.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cleveland-Cliffs' primary customers are in the North American automotive industry, which accounted for 32% of 2024 revenue, followed by infrastructure and manufacturing (27%), steel distributors and converters (28%), and other steel producers (13%). The company is a leading supplier of automotive-grade steel and also serves markets such as construction, appliances, energy, and electrical infrastructure.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in the United States and Canada, with major steelmaking and finishing facilities in Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Ontario. Its mining operations are located in Minnesota and Michigan, and it has a growing presence in Canada following the Stelco acquisition. Additional operations include scrap processing facilities in the Midwest and a small European distribution business.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cleveland-Cliffs is a vertically integrated steel producer, operating upstream (iron ore mining, pelletizing, HBI, coal mining), midstream (primary steelmaking via BF/BOF and EAF), and downstream (finishing, stamping, tooling, tubing, and scrap processing). This integration allows the company to control key raw materials and production processes, reducing reliance on external suppliers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include maintaining leadership in automotive steel, expanding into electrical steels for grid modernization and EVs, optimizing its integrated footprint for cost and carbon efficiency, and pursuing value-enhancing M&A (e.g., Stelco). R&D focuses on advanced steel grades, lightweighting, EV battery protection, and decarbonization technologies such as hydrogen use, direct reduced iron, and electrification of processes. The company is also investing in new transformer production and participating in DOE-funded decarbonization projects.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of steel products (flat-rolled, coated, electrical, stainless, plate, and tubular), iron ore pellets, HBI, scrap, and coke. Sales are made under a mix of annual fixed-price contracts (notably with automotive customers), index-linked contracts, and spot market transactions. The company also sells to third-party steel producers and distributors.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include domestic and foreign steel producers such as U.S. Steel, Nucor, and ArcelorMittal, as well as EAF-based producers and alternative material suppliers (e.g., aluminum). Cleveland-Cliffs is the largest supplier of automotive-grade steel in North America and the only fully integrated steelmaker with significant internal raw material sourcing. Its vertical integration and focus on high-end markets differentiate it from EAF-centric peers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Cleveland-Cliffs reported $19.2 billion in revenue, with approximately 30,000 employees. The company experienced a revenue decline of 13% year-over-year due to lower steel prices and volumes, resulting in a net loss of $708 million and adjusted EBITDA of $780 million. The recent acquisition of Stelco expands its scale and geographic reach, but the company is currently in a deleveraging phase following significant M&A activity.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cleveland-Cliffs emphasizes its unique vertical integration, which provides cost stability, supply chain security, and quality control from raw materials to finished steel. Its leadership in automotive-grade and electrical steels, technical support, and R&D capabilities enable it to meet demanding customer requirements. The company also highlights its commitment to environmental sustainability, labor partnerships, and its ability to offer the most comprehensive flat-rolled steel product selection in North America.
